facts.statement: The only known species of this genus is Canadaga arctica.
facts.quote: The single known species is Canadaga arctica.

facts.statement: Canadaga lived in the shallow seas near modern-day Bylot and Devon Islands in Nunavut, Canada.
facts.quote: It lived in the shallow seas around what today is Bylot and Devon Islands in Nunavut, Canada.

facts.statement: Fossils of Canadaga date to the Campanian to mid-Maastrichtian age, approximately 67 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in rocks dated to the Campanian to mid-Maastrichtian age, about 67 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossils of Canadaga were discovered in the Kanguk Formation.
facts.quote: It was found in the Kanguk Formation

facts.statement: Canadaga was a member of the Hesperornithes, a group of flightless, toothed seabirds from the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was a member of the Hesperornithes, flightless toothed seabirds of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Canadaga belonged to the family Hesperornithidae, which also includes the genus Hesperornis.
facts.quote: Among these, it belonged to the Hesperornithidae, along with Hesperornis, the well-known namesake genus.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives found in tropical waters, Canadaga seems to have lived in temperate or subarctic areas.
facts.quote: Unlike its relatives which are mainly known from subtropical or tropical waters, this species seems to have ranged in temperate or even subarctic areas.

facts.statement: The parent group of Canadaga is the family Hesperornithidae.
The time range for Canadaga spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
